as_told.title: Proposed project to clean the shafts with robots, with the University of Ferrara

plain: A team led by Filippo Biondi, a scientist who used radar from satellites to scan beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, is preparing a proposal to the Egyptian government for the Khafre Research Project, a study of the second great pyramid at Giza, together with the University of Ferrara in Italy and collaborators Armando Mei and Corrado Malanga. Biondi describes it himself across two appearances, first hoping the project can be "at the center" of the work, and later saying the plan is to clear shafts filled with debris using robots and to submit the proposal "these weeks." If it went ahead, it would let researchers check in person what the scans seem to show under the pyramid.
